audit.why: Disk chart (Skill, Shen, Shen, Skill, Skill, Shen, Shen) matches the packet chart and 54.9% over 1244 games; full and content agree row for row, and it does not contradict the already-audited tahmkench side.
Four spikes: Shen Lvl 2-3, Lvl 6 Stand United, first item, and Tahm Kench's late teamfight window. Timings hold; only the late spike's ability names were wrong (see point 4).

audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate errors. (a) 'Abyssal Voyage' is used as his ultimate in whys[6], spikes[3], late and wants.foe[2] — that ability is not in his kit; his W is Abyssal Dive and his R is Devour. (b) The stun is described as needing 'two hits' / 'two charges' (whys[0], whys[3], mid, early) — Tongue Lash stuns at THREE stacks of An Acquired Taste. (c) Thick Skin (E) is repeatedly called his 'grey-health passive'; his passive is An Acquired Taste. (d) The decisive interaction — what actually cancels Stand United — is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's kit: P An Acquired Taste (3 stacks arm Devour), Q Tongue Lash 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, slow + heal, stuns only when the target already has 3 stacks; W Abyssal Dive 21/20/19/18/17s with a knockup; E Thick Skin, 3s, stores damage as grey health and converts it to a shield; R Devour. The mirror audit on tahmkench__shen establishes that the 3-stack Tongue Lash stun and Abyssal Dive's knockup cancel Shen's R channel while a bare Tongue Lash slow does not.
audit.corrected: Ability names corrected throughout, the stun threshold set to three An Acquired Taste stacks, Thick Skin named as the grey-health source, and the Stand United cancel written into whys[3], breakdown.cooldowns and wants.foe[2] in the same terms the mirror uses.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid states 'Tongue Lash has a 5-second cooldown' — that is the rank-5 figure, not the lane-phase one. breakdown.cooldowns carries no numbers and never mentions Shen's own energy.
audit.why: Tongue Lash is 7s at rank 1. Shen's Q costs 140 energy and E costs 150 out of a 200 pool, so he only ever has one of them available — the mirror audit already identifies this as the real limiter on Shen's trade pattern.
audit.corrected: Rank-1 cooldowns written in and the energy constraint added.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late prescribes anti-heal without naming the sources.
audit.why: Tongue Lash heals him on champion hit and Thick Skin converts stored grey health into a shield every 3s — those two, not a passive, are what Grievous Wounds is timed against.

edits.before: At Level 1 both champions are passive — Tahm Kench wants to stack his Q (Tongue Lash) slow toward a stun and you want to position the spirit blade between you and him without overcommitting your E. Farm with empowered Q autos when the blade is in his face and back off before he gets two Tongue Lash stacks. At Level 2 Shadow Dash comes online: short-trade by E-taunting him into your W-zone, letting his forced autos land on nothing, then Q through the blade before leaving. He cannot devour out of the taunt and his grey-health passive only partially recovers between trades if you keep the tempo. At Level 3 the full pattern is live — W first to anchor the spirit blade, then E into it so his auto-attack chain burns on the refuge zone while your Twilight Assault triple autos deal bonus magic damage and his Ki Barrier shield absorbs the return. He has no burst to break through that window; he simply takes damage.
edits.after: At Level 1 both champions are passive — Tahm Kench wants to stack An Acquired Taste with Tongue Lash toward the three-stack stun and you want the spirit blade between you and him without overcommitting your E. Farm with empowered Q autos when the blade is in his face and back off at two stacks. At Level 2 Shadow Dash comes online: short-trade by E-taunting him into your W-zone, letting his forced autos land on nothing, then Q through the blade before leaving. He cannot devour out of the taunt and Thick Skin only converts part of the grey health if you keep the tempo up. At Level 3 the full pattern is live — W first to anchor the spirit blade, then E into it so his auto-attack chain burns on the refuge zone while your Twilight Assault triple autos deal bonus magic damage and your Ki Barrier shield absorbs the return. He has no burst to break that window; he simply takes damage.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are about managing his Q cooldown: Tongue Lash has a 5-second cooldown and he will try to stack two charges for the stun — never step up to trade right after he throws a Tongue Lash because a second is already cooking. Wait for both charges to be spent or the first to visibly be on cooldown before committing your Shadow Dash. At Level 6, Stand United changes everything in your favour. Tahm Kench is a lane-staller with zero mobility, so even if the lane is dead even you are now the more impactful champion — whenever a skirmish develops elsewhere, you teleport in with a free shield and potentially a 2v1. Use this to farm calmly, poke with Q when his blade is in position, and save E for either an all-in trade or a defensive interrupt if his jungler arrives.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are about managing his stacks: Tongue Lash is 7 seconds at rank 1 and only stuns once An Acquired Taste is at three — never step up to trade while you are sitting on two, because the next hit locks you down. Let the stacks fall off, or trade from zero, before committing your Shadow Dash. At Level 6, Stand United changes everything in your favour. Tahm Kench is a lane-staller with zero mobility, so even if the lane is dead even you are now the more impactful champion — whenever a skirmish develops elsewhere, you teleport in with a free shield and potentially a 2v1. Use this to farm calmly, poke with Q when the blade is in position, and save E for either an all-in trade or a defensive interrupt if his jungler arrives.

edits.before: In the late game Tahm Kench becomes a teamfight enabler through Abyssal Voyage roams and Devour peel, which means your Stand United value goes up equally — both ultimates are global or near-global disruption tools and the champion who uses theirs better wins the game. Keep burning Sunfire Aegis stacks in side-lane skirmishes to deny his grey-health reset loop, and respect his Devour in 5v5: he will swallow your carry to bodyblock your engage, so R onto a different target and taunt through his formation instead of charging in. Do not fight him at full HP near his tower — his sustained drain-tank pattern eventually tilts even in his favor once his build is complete, so rotate early and often rather than sitting in a lane he can never lose outright.
edits.after: In the late game Tahm Kench becomes a teamfight enabler through Devour peel and Abyssal Dive engage, which means your Stand United value goes up equally — his disruption is local and yours reaches the whole map, so the champion who spends theirs better wins the game. Keep burning Sunfire Aegis stacks in side-lane skirmishes to deny his Thick Skin conversion, and respect his Devour in 5v5: he will swallow your carry to bodyblock your engage, so R onto a different target and taunt through his formation instead of charging in. Do not fight him at full HP near his tower — his drain-tank pattern eventually tilts in his favor once his build is complete, so rotate early and often rather than sitting in a lane he can never lose outright.
